classification.habit: Perennial rhizomatous herb with leafy pseudostems 30–90 cm tall.
classification.habitat: Cultivated in warm, humid tropical areas on well-drained loamy soil.
classification.distribution: Cultivated throughout India, chiefly in Kerala, Karnataka, Odisha, Meghalaya and the North-East.

identification.description: Dried, buff to light-grey, branched rhizome with characteristic aromatic pungency.
identification.whole_plant: Herb with an aromatic branched rhizome and erect leafy shoots formed of rolled leaf sheaths.
identification.root: Fibrous adventitious roots arise from the lower surface of the rhizome.
identification.stem: The true stem is the horizontal rhizome: laterally compressed, with short flattish ovate branches on the upper side, buff coloured externally with longitudinal striations, fracture short, aromatic and pungent (API); aerial shoot is a pseudostem of leaf sheaths.
identification.leaf: Distichous, linear-lanceolate, sessile leaves 15–30 cm long with sheathing bases.
identification.flower: Flowers in dense cone-like spikes on a separate scape; corolla greenish-yellow with a purple lip; flowering is rare in cultivation.
identification.fruit: Fruit is a capsule, rarely formed in cultivation.
identification_points: Short fracture showing scattered vascular bundles and yellow secretory cells

therapeutics.anupana: Ushna jala (warm water); with Guda in Amavata
therapeutics.precautions: Ushna-Tikshna drug: use cautiously in Pitta-predominant states, Raktapitta, Amlapitta, Daha and bleeding tendencies, and in summer. Large doses may cause heartburn.
therapeutics.contraindications: Raktapitta and active bleeding, severe Amlapitta and peptic ulcer, Pittaja Jwara with burning; use cautiously with anticoagulant medicines.

shlokas:
शुण्ठी रुच्यामवातघ्नी पाचनी कटुका लघुः ।
स्निग्धोष्णा मधुरा पाके कफवातविबन्धनुत् ॥४५॥
nighantu_references: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu, Haritakyadi Varga, verse 45; related therapeutic continuation in verse 46. Independently searchable recension; edition numbering may vary.
reference_hubs: TDU Indian Medicinal Plants Database — Shlokas

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Pungency is due to gingerols, which convert to the more pungent shogaols on drying; the aroma comes from the sesquiterpene-rich essential oil.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Dry ginger is known as the 'universal medicine'. It aids digestion, reduces inflammation, and pacifies Vata and Kapha.
recognized_uses: Nausea and vomiting, including motion sickness
modern_information.safety_notes: Generally safe in culinary amounts; higher doses can cause heartburn and may add to the effect of anticoagulant and antiplatelet drugs.

exam_points: Botanical name: Zingiber officinale Roscoe; Family: Zingiberaceae
Useful part: dried rhizome (Shunthi); fresh rhizome is Ardraka
Rasa: Katu; Guna: Laghu, Snigdha; Virya: Ushna; Vipaka: Madhura
Karma: Deepana, Pachana, Anulomana, Amadoshahara, Vatakaphahara (API)
Formulations: Trikatu Churna, Saubhagya Shunthi, Vaishvanara Churna
viva_questions: What is the difference between Shunthi and Ardraka?
Which compounds give ginger its pungency?
student.quick_revision: Dry ginger is known as the 'universal medicine'. It aids digestion, reduces inflammation, and pacifies Vata and Kapha.

teaching_points: Contrast Shunthi (dry) and Ardraka (fresh) in properties and uses.
Explain the exception: Katu rasa with Madhura vipaka and Snigdha guna.
Show Shunthi as the key Amapachana drug in Amavata.
discussion_points: Why Shunthi is Vrishya and Snigdha unlike other Katu dravyas
Evidence for ginger in nausea and vomiting
practical_points: Examine rhizome pieces for shape, colour, fracture, odour and taste.
Prepare Trikatu Churna in the pharmacy practical.

doctor.quick_reference: Shunthi (Katu, Ushna, Madhura vipaka, Laghu-Snigdha) is the chief Deepana-Pachana and Amapachana drug for Agnimandya, Amavata, Adhmana and Kapha-Vata disorders; 1–2 g churna.
doctor.anupana: Ushna jala (warm water); with Guda in Amavata
key_precautions: Caution in Pitta states and Raktapitta
